    <summary>The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. Additionally, HyperVQ represents codebook vectors as geometric representatives of hyperbolic decision hyperplanes, encouraging disentangled and robust latent representations. Our experiments demonstrate that HyperVQ matches traditional VQ in generative and reconstruction tasks, while surpassing it in discriminative performance and yielding a more efficient and disentangled codebook.</summary>

    <title>Geometry-Aware Hyperbolic Residual-Quantized Variational Autoencoders</title>
    <updated>2026-09-25T14:21:51Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26342v2" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.26342v2" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. Hyperbolic geometry offers a natural alternative for hierarchical representations, but naive hyperbolic extensions introduce geometric inconsistencies: non-associative hyperbolic addition prevents consistent residual aggregation, while standard straight-through gradient estimation ignores the geometry of the latent space. We propose a geometry-aware hyperbolic residual quantization that addresses these issues in both the forward and backward passes. In the forward pass, Hyperbolic Residual Aggregation restores the telescoping behavior of residual quantization on the Poincare ball. In the backward pass, a discounted Hyperbolic Straight-Through Estimator routes the reconstruction gradient through the quantizer as a single geometric block, avoiding unstable recursive gradient transport across residual stages. Evaluations on hierarchical prediction, recommendation, image tokenization, and neural audio coding tasks show that our method improves the stability and structural organization of hyperbolic residual codes over naive hyperbolic baselines. At the same time, we observe a clear structure-compression trade-off: Euclidean residual quantization remains preferable for pure compression, while geometry-aware hyperbolic quantization is most useful for hierarchically organized discrete latent spaces.</summary>

    <summary>  We describe the space of (all) invariant deformation quantizations on the hyperbolic plane as solutions of the evolution of a second order hyperbolic differential operator.     <title>Catenaries and minimal surfaces of revolution in hyperbolic space</title>
    <updated>2023-06-11T17:28:18Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.15297v2" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.15297v2" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We introduce the concept of extrinsic catenary in the hyperbolic plane. Working in the hyperboloid model, we define an extrinsic catenary as the shape of a curve hanging under its weight as seen from the ambient space. In other words, an extrinsic catenary is a critical point of the potential functional, where we calculate the potential with the extrinsic distance to a fixed reference plane in the ambient Lorentzian space. We then characterize extrinsic catenaries in terms of their curvature and as a solution to a prescribed curvature problem involving certain vector fields. In addition, we prove that the generating curve of any minimal surface of revolution in the hyperbolic space is an extrinsic catenary with respect to an appropriate reference plane. Finally, we prove that one of the families of extrinsic catenaries admits an intrinsic characterization if we replace the extrinsic distance with the intrinsic length of horocycles orthogonal to a reference geodesic.</summary>

    <updated>2024-01-14T06:32:14Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.07212v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.07212v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Existing unsupervised deep product quantization methods primarily aim for the increased similarity between different views of the identical image, whereas the delicate multi-level semantic similarities preserved between images are overlooked. Moreover, these methods predominantly focus on the Euclidean space for computational convenience, compromising their ability to map the multi-level semantic relationships between images effectively. To mitigate these shortcomings, we propose a novel unsupervised product quantization method dubbed \textbf{Hi}erarchical \textbf{H}yperbolic \textbf{P}roduct \textbf{Q}uantization (HiHPQ), which learns quantized representations by incorporating hierarchical semantic similarity within hyperbolic geometry. Specifically, we propose a hyperbolic product quantizer, where the hyperbolic codebook attention mechanism and the quantized contrastive learning on the hyperbolic product manifold are introduced to expedite quantization. Furthermore, we propose a hierarchical semantics learning module, designed to enhance the distinction between similar and non-matching images for a query by utilizing the extracted hierarchical semantics as an additional training supervision. Experiments on benchmarks show that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.</summary>

    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2509.26117v2</id>
    <title>Partially hyperbolic flows on flat vector bundles with an application to complete affine manifolds</title>
    <updated>2026-02-16T10:52:17Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.26117v2" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.26117v2" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Let $N$ be a manifold of dimension $m$ with a flat vector bundle given by a representation $ρ:π_1(N) \rightarrow \mathrm{GL}(n, \mathbf{R})$ where $π_1(N)$ is finitely generated. The holonomy group $ρ$ is a $k$-partially hyperbolic holonomy representation if the flat bundle pulled back over the unit tangent bundle of a sufficiently large compact submanifold of $N$ splits into expanding, neutral, and contracting subbundles along the geodesic flow, where the expanding and contracting subbundles are $k$-dimensional with $k < n/2$. Suppose that each element of $ρ(π_1(N))$ has an eigenvalue of norm $1$, or, alternatively, $ρ$ has some singular values of subexponential growth in terms of word length. We show that $ρ$ is a $P$-Anosov representation for a parabolic subgroup $P$ of $\mathrm{GL}(n, \mathbf{R})$ if and only if $ρ$ is a partially hyperbolic representation. We are going to primarily employ representation theory techniques. As an application, we will show that the equivalence holds when $N$ is a complete affine $n$-manifold, and $ρ$ is a linear part of the holonomy representation. This had never been done over the full general linear group.</summary>
    <category term="math.GT" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <category term="math.RT" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2025-09-30T11:36:37Z</published>
    <arxiv:comment>22 pages. This paper generalizes Part 1 of "Complete affine manifolds with Anosov holonomy groups,'' ArXiv:2009.11127, and Part 2 is dropped. The main setting has changed over to flat vector bundles. This involved many changes. Part 2 is still available at ArXiv:2009.11127. Furthermore, we generalized the premise of the main theorem to include a subexponential growth condition on singular values</arxiv:comment>
    <arxiv:primary_category term="math.GT"/>

Specify transport path, curvature/domain, finite precision, zero-vector handling, and comparison tolerance; avoid reducing the score to an identity or duplicating the closed transported-residual family.
+4. **Geodesic margin under a frozen triplet constraint.** Among code candidates, prefer the one maximizing the worst-case hyperbolic separation between the item and a frozen positive/negative neighbor pair, with the pair list computed from the original training split only. This is a selection-time operation, not a downstream reranker. Measure how often the constraint changes assignments and its per-level rate before proposing it. Fix empty-pair behavior, distance clamps, finite score tolerance, and tie order in advance.
+
+### Mandatory gate before selecting one
+
+For each idea, provide an executable-from-frozen-artifacts occurrence-rate definition (including denominator and per-level counts) and compute it before training or implementation. For every operator, predeclare: model/domain and valid inputs; dtype; epsilons and clamps; iteration/termination rules if applicable; NaN/Inf and boundary behavior; score comparison tolerance; and deterministic tie-breaking. If the measurable event is negligible, or these semantics cannot be made finite-precision complete, do not advance the candidate. Any eventual claim must be tested against all three frozen strict inequalities: Hard-L1 ER > 16.38953942232631, Stage3 Recall@10 > 0.06406796775709883, and NDCG@10 > 0.03530651701940677.
*** End Patch

    <summary>The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability. Additionally, HyperVQ represents codebook vectors as geometric representatives of hyperbolic decision hyperplanes, encouraging disentangled and robust latent representations. Our experiments demonstrate that HyperVQ matches traditional VQ in generative and reconstruction tasks, while surpassing it in discriminative performance and yielding a more efficient and disentangled codebook.</summary>

+
+## Candidate mechanism ideas not occupied by the inspected abstracts
+
+These are deliberately hypotheses, not novelty or performance claims. Each places a non-trivial hyperbolic operation in the *selection* of an integer code, rather than changing the frozen recipes. Before implementation, specify all arithmetic and boundary semantics in finite precision, then measure the relevant occurrence rate directly from frozen assignment artifacts (no training). Reject any idea whose operative event is too rare.
+
+1. **Karcher-centroid marginal assignment.** For each candidate code at a level, evaluate the decrease in a bounded-support Fréchet/Karcher objective of the item's fixed neighborhood after assigning it to that code; choose the greatest decrease, with deterministic code-ID tie resolution. This is not ordinary point-to-codeword distance or hyperbolic MLR. Pre-measure how often this neighborhood correction changes the nearest-code assignment. Finite-precision declaration must fix the ball/domain, iteration count, convergence tolerance, and behavior on non-convergence.
+2. **Hyperbolic Voronoi-boundary margin.** Select by signed geodesic distance to a candidate code’s decision boundary (not codeword radius/distance), optionally weighted by a fixed, frozen local density estimate. Measure the fraction of assignments whose selected code changes versus the frozen rule. Define boundary ties and margin clamps explicitly.

This is a selection-time operation, not a downstream reranker. Measure how often the constraint changes assignments and its per-level rate before proposing it. Fix empty-pair behavior, distance clamps, finite score tolerance, and tie order in advance.
